subject: DPA: jurisdictional scoping & SCCs mapping — NimbusCare order form
messages:
From: Simon Palmer <simon.palmer@nimbuscare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA / SCCs questions for NimbusCare order form

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and security at NimbusCare reviewed the draft MSA + Order Form you sent and have a few open items on the DPA side before we can sign:

- SCCs mapping: we need an explicit Annex B mapping for subprocessors and a clear statement of which SCCs variant applies for analytics and model inference.
- Roles & responsibilities: the draft Order Form currently lists Redwood as "processor" but our counsel is asking for additional language that clarifies controller/processor boundaries when NimbusCare provides patient-supplied content.
- KMS / encryption: we require clarity on whether Redwood can support a customer-managed KMS key for EU-hosted deployments (we have a firm requirement for BYOK for regulated datasets).
- Export & transfer impact: if Redwood performs any downstream model training or re-use of customer data for RL/analytics, we need a carveout/exclusion or explicit guarantee.

Attached is our suggested redline for the DPA and an SCCs mapping spreadsheet — can you confirm who on your side will lead redline reconciliation and whether Redwood has an EU-only hosting commitment in the order form?

Attachments: [Attachment: Nimbus_DPA_redline_v1.docx (document)], [Attachment: SCCs_mapping_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Simon
Simon Palmer
Head of Security & Privacy — NimbusCare

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Palmer <simon.palmer@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nimbuscare.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs questions for NimbusCare order form

Hi Simon — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Looping in our Legal lead (Laura) and Privacy/Compliance (Ben) to reconcile. Quick answers up front:

- Hosting / residency: we can commit to an EU-only hosting option in the order form (EU region only) as a capacity/plan option; I will confirm the exact billing SKU and any cost delta.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments and VPCs; we need to check the SLA and key rotation language for the hosted plan you selected.
- Model training / reuse: Redwood's hosted default is not to train on customer data without explicit consent; we can add explicit language prohibiting reuse for model training and analytics unless agreed.

Laura / Ben — can you take Nimbus's redline and propose a reconciled DPA (track-changes) that addresses: (a) Annex B/SCCs mapping, (b) explicit BYOK/KMS language for EU-only hosting, and (c) a narrow export carveout definition (if any required)? Preferably return a consolidated redline by EOD Monday so Nimbus can run it through their security ops.

Simon — would a 30-minute call on Monday be useful to walk the two sides through the redline?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Palmer <simon.palmer@nimbuscare.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA / SCCs questions for NimbusCare order form

Marissa / team — taking this on. Summary of our approach (details in attached redline):

1) SCCs / Annex B: we accept providing a completed Annex B mapping the processing activities to the SCCs modules (Controller-to-Processor scenario) but will include language clarifying that the applicable SCCs variant is determined by the role in each engagement (Order Form Exhibit will capture per-product role).

2) Roles & liability: propose clearer role language and a short schedule that maps product features to controller/processor responsibilities (will be an exhibit to the Order Form). This avoids re-opening the MSA core trade-offs while giving Nimbus the contractual certainty they need.

3) KMS/BYOK: propose two paths: (A) Private/VPC: full BYOK support and key control language; (B) Hosted EU SKU: customer key wrapping with managed rotation and an SLA note. We'll surface the precise SLA delta and whether HSM-backed keys are required for NimbusCare.

4) Export & model training: propose a default prohibition on using customer content for model training or aggregated analytics without explicit opt-in. For telemetry/ops we will add an allowable minimal-exception clause (anonymized telemetry for service stability only) with strict pseudonymization and retention limits.

5) Subprocessor notification: propose a 15-day advance notice and a customer approval step for high-risk subprocessors (or an allow-list process), captured in the DPA Exhibit.

I've attached a consolidated redline and an SCCs mapping workbook with our suggested Annex B entries. Please review and advise if Nimbus wants any of the above moved to a separate Transfer Impact Addendum.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_v2.docx (document)], [Attachment: SCCs_Annex_mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Simon Palmer <simon.palmer@nimbuscare.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs questions for NimbusCare order form

Laura — really appreciate the concise approach and the BYOK options. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after a quick read:

- The model training prohibition is critical. Can you confirm "no training on customer content" is drafted as unconditional for the hosted plan unless a separate written agreement is signed? Their ask is a one-sentence contractual guarantee.
- For the hosted EU SKU, please clarify if Redwood will retain any key escrow capability (we need to know whether Redwood can access keys under operational scenarios).
- Export carveout: our data governance team wants a tighter definition of "anonymized telemetry" and a maximum retention (preferably no more than 90 days).

We will need to run Redwood_DPA_response_v2.docx by our counsel; can we have a 48-hour turnaround on any follow-ups? Happy to schedule the call after that check.

Thanks,
Simon

Simon / Elena —

Thanks for the quick read-through and the clarifying asks. Short answers and next steps:

- "No training on customer content" — confirmed. We will include a single-sentence contractual guarantee in the DPA for the hosted plan: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve models used in its production services without Customer's prior written consent."

- Key access / escrow: for the hosted EU SKU we do not retain master key escrow rights. For Private/VPC we support HSM-backed BYOK where Redwood cannot access plaintext keys. I'll have Ben surface the exact host-SKU language for the order form exhibit.

- Telemetry retention: we will propose a 90-day max for anonymized operational telemetry used solely for service stability and will include the pseudonymization process in an annex.

Action items:
- Laura: finalize consolidated redline (Redwood_DPA_response_v2.docx) with the single-sentence training clause and explicit BYOK/escrow language, then place the redline in the shared Drive folder.
- Ben: draft the Order Form Exhibit for EU-only hosting SKU and the BYOK billing note; include the expected cost delta.
- Marissa (me): schedule a 30-minute legal ops call for Fri 2025-05-16 09:00 CEST / 00:00 PDT (adjust if needed) to walk NimbusCare through the redline.

Simon — please confirm if 48 hours is enough after we post the final redline (we expect to upload by EOB Thursday 2025-05-15). Once Nimbus signs off we will send a DocuSign package for the Order Form + DPA.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
